assumptions: Chassis frame dimensions assumed to provide mounting points for front suspension.
Uprights positioned at typical front axle location relative to engine.
Control arm angles approximated for double-wishbone geometry.
Rotors are 320mm diameter (160mm radius) typical for sports car front axle.
Calipers are fixed type for better pedal feel and performance.
Master cylinder is mounted centrally on the firewall/bulkhead area.

Wheel rims are 18-inch diameter (approx 457mm OD, modeled as 400mm radius for visual proportion relative to 320mm rotors, actually 200mm radius is 400mm diameter which is ~15.7 inches, let's adjust to 225mm radius for 18 inch approx 450mm). Wait, 18 inches is 457mm. Radius 228mm. Let's use 230mm radius for rim. Tire adds sidewall. 230mm rim radius. Tire outer radius approx 260mm for low profile? No, 230mm is radius. Diameter 460mm. Tire adds maybe 30-40mm radius. Let's say Rim Radius 230, Tire Radius 265.
Rim width 180mm (7 inches) typical for front sports car.
Steering rack is mounted centrally below the engine/transmission tunnel.
Tie rods connect to the uprights at a point roughly aligned with the wheel center height.
Rack travel and pinion ratio are not modeled, only static geometry.
not_verified: Nothing here has been analysed or checked. There is no solver and no interference check in this deployment — this is a shape, not a result.
Mounting points are approximate and may not align perfectly with upright interfaces.
Hydraulic line routing is simplified straight runs; real cars use complex bends and clips.
Caliper mounting brackets are not modeled explicitly, assumed integrated or bolted to upright.
Brake pad clearance within caliper is not verified.
Wheel bolt pattern and hub centricity not modeled.
Tire sidewall stiffness and deformation not simulated.
Steering geometry (Ackermann, bump steer) is not analyzed.
Clearance between tie rods and suspension arms during articulation is not verified.
Mounting brackets for the rack to the chassis are simplified as direct placement.
